title: ISS Pro Evolution
subtitle: Football becomes a continuing club project

body: ISS Pro Evolution is Konami Computer Entertainment Tokyo's PlayStation football game, first released in Japan on 2 September 1999. It develops the series' on-field play while introducing club sides and the Master League. A match can now belong to a longer campaign in which a team is built and improved, giving the next fixture a context beyond an isolated victory. The clubs use city-based names rather than full official branding, but their role is clear. They turn the football game into something that can be returned to as an ongoing season and a personal project.

On the field, movement and passing create opportunities that a direct run towards goal may not provide. The player learns to recognise space, bring another teammate into the move and choose when to attempt the final ball. Club squads and international teams give different groups through which to practise those decisions. The largely unlicensed names and emblems mean presentation does not exactly reproduce the real competitions, but the relationships between players remain the centre of the experience. A good attack is assembled through several coordinated actions rather than one spectacular input.

The original Master League includes sixteen club teams, making it a compact foundation for a feature that would become closely associated with Pro Evolution Soccer. Its progression gives results and team choices a continuing importance between matches. European and North American releases followed in 2000. The music is credited to a team including Akira Yamaoka and Shinji Enomoto. The game's significance lies partly in this shift of scale: football on the console becomes both the ninety-minute contest being played and the longer work of developing a team worth returning to.
